Pedosphere Theory

Scope, process inventory, and certificate map

The RELIC pedosphere domain (relic.scientific.pedosphere) represents litter and soil organic carbon turnover, cross-sphere litterfall and hydrological chain maps, soil nitrogen mineralization, nitrification, denitrification, and leaching, root nitrogen and phosphorus uptake, diagnostic C:N stoichiometry auditing, wetland methane production, oxidation, three-pathway transport, and single-owner budget realization, as well as porous-media water, gas, solute, Freundlich index-1 equilibrium-sorption DAE, moving-domain ALE diffusion, and mobile-immobile two-region mass transfer (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapter 23).

Twenty-four concrete scientific Functors reside in relic.scientific.pedosphere, each paired with an IPHSEquivalenceCertificate spanning Level 1 (3 classes), Level 2 (13 classes), and Level 3 (8 classes):

General conservation ledgers follow Mathematical Foundations, discrete cochain operators follow DEC, IPHS, and GENERIC, and DAE, ALE, and splitting contracts follow Numerical Methods.

Soil organic carbon turnover and cross-sphere interface maps

Five-pool observation and mutually exclusive decomposition closures

On the canonical five-pool areal carbon vector \(\mathbf{C} = (C_{\mathrm{met}}, C_{\mathrm{str}}, C_{\mathrm{fast}}, C_{\mathrm{slow}}, C_{\mathrm{passive}})^{\mathsf{T}}\) [g C m\(^{-2}\)], CarbonPoolsFunctor (Level 1) evaluates the per-cell total \(C_{\mathrm{total}}(c) = \sum_i C_i(c)\) across the pool axis without summing across unequal-area grid cells or modifying stocks (\(\Delta \mathbf{C} = \mathbf{0}\)).

A simulation graph selects at most one prognostic decomposition owner for a given soil carbon support (Parton et al., 1987; Coleman and Jenkinson, 1996; Wieder et al., 2013):

  1. Compartment matrix (PoolsMatrix, Level 2): with diagonal turnover matrix \(K\) [s\(^{-1}\)], column-sub-stochastic transfer matrix \(T\) (\(T_{ij} \ge 0\), \(\sum_i T_{ij} \le 1\)), environmental scalar \(f_{\mathrm{env}}\), and litter input vector \(\mathbf{I}\) [g C m\(^{-2}\) s\(^{-1}\)],

    \[\mathbf{D} = f_{\mathrm{env}} K \mathbf{C}, \qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{C}}{\mathrm{d}t} = (T - I_d)\mathbf{D} + \mathbf{I}, \qquad R_{\mathrm{hetero}} = \mathbf{1}^{\mathsf{T}}(I_d - T)\mathbf{D},\]

    satisfying the exact open carbon ledger \(\sum_i \Delta C_i + R_{\mathrm{hetero}}\Delta t - \sum_i I_i\Delta t = 0\).

  2. Pool-resolved first-order kinetics (FirstOrderDecomposition, Level 2): replaces scalar \(f_{\mathrm{env}}K\) with pool-specific decay rates \(D_i = k_i\,f_T(T)\,f_\theta(\theta)\,f_{q,i}\,C_i\) under \(Q_{10}\) or Arrhenius thermal scaling and clay/lignin stabilization modifiers \(f_{q,i}\), closing the same five-pool carbon and \(R_{\mathrm{hetero}}\) ledger.

  3. Reverse Michaelis-Menten microbial-enzyme kinetics (MicrobialEnzymeDecomposition, Level 2): couples substrate pools \(S_i\) [g C m\(^{-2}\)] to active microbial biomass \(M_{\mathrm{mic}}\) [g C m\(^{-2}\)] with carbon-use efficiency \(\mathrm{CUE} \in (0, 1)\):

    \[V_i = \frac{M_{\mathrm{mic}}\,V_{\max,i}(T, \theta)\,S_i}{K_{m,i}(T) + M_{\mathrm{mic}}}, \qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}M_{\mathrm{mic}}}{\mathrm{d}t} = \mathrm{CUE}\sum_i V_i - D_{\mathrm{mic}}, \qquad R_{\mathrm{microbial}} = (1 - \mathrm{CUE})\sum_i V_i + D_{\mathrm{mic}},\]

    where \(D_{\mathrm{mic}} = (\tau_{\mathrm{turn}} + \tau_{\mathrm{maint}}f_T)M_{\mathrm{mic}}\) so \(\sum_i \Delta S_i + \Delta M_{\mathrm{mic}} + R_{\mathrm{microbial}}\Delta t = 0\) prior to external litter addition.

Litterfall and hydrological chain maps

LitterfallInterfaceMapper (Level 2) partitions plant litter and livestock dung inputs onto metabolic and structural litter ports while preserving total C and N mass: \(F_{\mathrm{met,C}} + F_{\mathrm{str,C}} = F_{\mathrm{plant,C}} + F_{\mathrm{dung,C}}\) and \(F_{\mathrm{org,N}} = F_{\mathrm{plant,N}} + F_{\mathrm{dung,N}}\). PedosphereInterfaceMapper (Level 2) projects hydrological boundary fluxes (infiltration, evapotranspiration, drainage) onto pedosphere port names via the identity chain map \(\mathbf{y}_h = I_3\mathbf{x}_h\) (REPLACE) without recomputing hydrological closures.

Soil nitrogen, root P uptake, and C:N stoichiometry boundaries

Mineralization, nitrification, denitrification, aggregation, and leaching

  1. Mineralization and immobilization (MineralizationProcess, Level 2): bounds gross organic-N mineralization and microbial \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\) immobilization against available stocks over \(\Delta t\):

    \[R_{\mathrm{gross}} = \min\!\left(k_{\min} N_{\mathrm{org}} f_{\mathrm{env}},\; \frac{N_{\mathrm{org}}}{\Delta t}\right), \qquad R_{\mathrm{immob}} = \min\!\left(\frac{\mathrm{CUE}\cdot \mathrm{DEC}}{\mathrm{CN}_{\mathrm{mic}}\,\eta_N},\; \frac{N_{\mathrm{NH_4}}}{\Delta t}\right),\]

    preserving \(\Delta N_{\mathrm{org}} + \Delta N_{\mathrm{NH_4}} + \Delta N_{\mathrm{mic}} = 0\) on internal transformations.

  2. Nitrification (NitrificationProcess, Level 2) and denitrification (DenitrificationProcess, Level 2): both consume water_filled_pore_space \(W \in [0, 1]\) (Linn and Doran, 1984; Del Grosso et al., 2000) under documented RELIC piecewise-linear oxygen and anaerobic ramps (\(W_{\mathrm{opt}} = W_{\mathrm{thr}} = 0.6\), minimum floor \(0.1\)):

    \[r_{\mathrm{nit}} = V_{\max,\mathrm{nit}}\,\frac{N_{\mathrm{NH_4}}}{K_{m,\mathrm{NH_4}} + N_{\mathrm{NH_4}}}\,f_T\,f_{\mathrm{pH}}\,f_{\mathrm{O_2}}(W), \qquad r_{\mathrm{denit}} = V_{\max,\mathrm{denit}}\,\frac{N_{\mathrm{NO_3}}}{K_{m,\mathrm{NO_3}} + N_{\mathrm{NO_3}}}\,f_{\mathrm{anaer}}(W)\,f_C\,f_T\,f_{\mathrm{pH}},\]

    closing local nitrogen mass ledgers \(\Delta N_{\mathrm{NH_4}} + \Delta N_{\mathrm{NO_3}} + \Delta N_{\mathrm{N_2O,nit}} = 0\) and \(\Delta N_{\mathrm{NO_3}} + \Delta N_{\mathrm{N_2O,denit}} + \Delta N_{\mathrm{N_2}} = 0\).

  3. Diagnostic N aggregation (NitrogenCycling, Level 2) and retarded leaching (NitrogenLeachingProcess, Level 3): NitrogenCycling aggregates child process rates diagnostically without re-running child kinetics and commits only the external fertilizer-plus-urine ammonium increment \(\Delta N_{\mathrm{NH_4,ext}} = 1000(F_{\mathrm{fert}} + F_{\mathrm{urine}})\Delta t\) via UpdateItem(ACCUMULATE, per_timestep=True). NitrogenLeachingProcess computes drainage-driven export from mobile retarded nitrate concentration \(C_{\mathrm{NO_3,mob}} = \frac{N_{\mathrm{NO_3}}/(\theta z_s)}{1 + \rho_b K_d / \theta}\) and water drainage \(F_w\), bounded by pool availability and minimum depletion timescale so \(\Delta N_{\mathrm{NO_3}} + F_{N,\mathrm{leach}}\Delta t = 0\).

Root N and P uptake and C:N diagnostic scope

relic.scientific.pedosphere.nutrient_cycling.root_nutrient_uptake.RootNutrientUptake (Level 2) evaluates layered Michaelis-Menten root uptake \(U_i(z) = V_{\max,i}\frac{C_i(z)}{K_{m,i} + C_i(z)} f_T f_W W_{\mathrm{root}}(z)\) (Barber, 1995) for \(\mathrm{NO_3^-}\), \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\), and dissolved phosphorus. Molar plant nitrogen storage \(S_N\) [mol N m\(^{-2}\)] and gram-basis soil pools \(m_{\mathrm{NO_3}}, m_{\mathrm{NH_4}}\) [g N m\(^{-2}\)] close via \((\Delta m_{\mathrm{NO_3}} + \Delta m_{\mathrm{NH_4}})/M_N + \Delta S_N = 0\). Realized molar phosphorus uptake rate \(U_P\) [mol P m\(^{-2}\) s\(^{-1}\)] is bounded by a four-way minimum over kinetic uptake capacity \(U_{P,\mathrm{kin}}\), plant demand \(D_P\), available labile soil phosphorus \(P_{\mathrm{avail}}\) [g P m\(^{-2}\)], and remaining plant P storage capacity \(P_{\mathrm{cap,mol}}\) [mol P m\(^{-2}\)]:

\[ U_P = \min\!\left(U_{P,\mathrm{kin}},\; D_P,\; \frac{P_{\mathrm{avail}}}{M_P\,\Delta t},\; \frac{P_{\mathrm{cap,mol}}}{\Delta t}\right), \qquad \Delta P_{\mathrm{avail}} + \Delta P_{\mathrm{plant}} = 0. \]

Phosphorus and stoichiometry scope boundary: RootNutrientUptake (together with managed phosphate delivery from FertilizationManagement and foliar N:P limitation in NutrientStress) constitutes the implemented [I] phosphorus interface. Standalone multi-pool soil phosphorus weathering, occlusion, mineralization, and P-leaching Functors remain [N]. Separately, relic.scientific.pedosphere.nutrient_cycling.stoichiometry.StoichiometryConstraint (Level 1, ScaleCouplingFunctor) is a read-only C:N flux-ratio and mass-balance diagnostic observer (\(\Delta \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}\)); it neither projects state onto a stoichiometric manifold nor audits phosphorus pools.

Wetland methane request-and-coupler architecture

To prevent competing storage clamps across methanogenesis, methanotrophy, and three-pathway gas escape, RELIC separates wetland \(\mathrm{CH_4}\) into three stateless tendency/request Functors, one prognostic budget owner, and one diagnostic scale-routing observer:

  1. Production request (MethaneProductionFunctor, Level 2): blends the iMAPLE inundation branch (Yue et al., 2024, Eq. 34) and a redox-gated calibrated branch with gating weight \(w \in [0, 1]\) and peaked temperature response \(f_{ST}(T)\) (Zhu et al., 2014):

    \[P_{\mathrm{CH_4}} = (1 - w)\,R_h r f_{ST}(T) f_{\mathrm{pH}} f_{\mathrm{wet}} + w\,R_h r f_{ST}(T) f_{Eh}(Eh)\,A.\]

  2. Oxidation request (MethaneOxidationFunctor, Level 2): evaluates dual Michaelis-Menten kinetics in porewater \(\mathrm{CH_4}\) and \(\mathrm{O_2}\) concentrations (Riley et al., 2011, Eq. 7; Oleson et al., 2013, Eq. 19.11), bounded by \(M_{\mathrm{CH_4}}/\Delta t\).

  3. Three-pathway transport request (MethaneTransportFunctor, Level 3): sums aqueous-gaseous molecular diffusion \(F_{\mathrm{diff}}\), threshold ebullition \(F_{\mathrm{ebull}}\), and aerenchyma plant-mediated venting \(F_{\mathrm{plant}}\) (Walter and Heimann, 2000) into \(F_{\mathrm{req}} = F_{\mathrm{diff}} + F_{\mathrm{ebull}} + F_{\mathrm{plant}}\) and \(T_{\mathrm{trans}} = -F_{\mathrm{req}}\) (REPLACE).

  4. Single realization owner (MethaneBudgetCoupler, Level 2): integrates combined tendencies \(\Delta M_{\mathrm{raw}} = (T_{\mathrm{prod}} + T_{\mathrm{oxid}} + T_{\mathrm{trans}})\Delta t\), enforces non-negativity once via \(\Delta M = \max(\Delta M_{\mathrm{raw}}, -M_{\mathrm{CH_4}})\), commits \(\Delta M\) to ch4_soil_storage (ACCUMULATE, per_timestep=True), and deducts any storage-limiter deficit \(R_{\mathrm{lim}} = (\Delta M - \Delta M_{\mathrm{raw}})/\Delta t\) from realized atmospheric emission \(F_{\mathrm{atm}} = F_{\mathrm{req}} - R_{\mathrm{lim}}\) so \(\Delta M + (O - P_{\mathrm{CH_4}} + F_{\mathrm{atm}})\Delta t = 0\). MethaneScaleCouplingFunctor (Level 1) computes the bounded diagnostic routing weight \(w_{\mathrm{DNDC}} = \operatorname{clip}(\alpha_{\mathrm{wet}}f_{\mathrm{wet}} + \alpha_{\mathrm{wfps}}W + \alpha_{\mathrm{data}}s_{\mathrm{data}} - \tau,\; 0,\; 1)\).

Porous-media water, gas, solute, DAE, ALE, and memory transport

Richards water, Millington-Quirk gas diffusion, and retarded solute transport

  • SoilWaterTransportFunctor (Level 3) solves the 1D mixed Richards balance \(\partial_t \theta = -\partial_z q + S\) with \(q = -K(\theta)\partial_z(h + z)\) in discrete cochain form \(\dot{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_h = -D_h \mathbf{q}_h + G_h \mathbf{u}_h\) (\(\star_K = \star_K^{\mathsf{T}} \succeq 0\)), emitting full next-state soil_moisture via REPLACE.

  • GasDiffusion1D (Level 3) diffuses vadose \(\mathrm{CO_2}\)-C and \(\mathrm{N_2O}\)-N profiles under Millington and Quirk (1961) tortuosity above a no-flux lower boundary (ACCUMULATE concentration increments, REPLACE surface efflux).

  • SoluteAdvectionDiffusion1D (Level 3) solves 1D retarded advection-dispersion \(\partial_t\left((\theta + \rho_b K_d)C\right) = -\partial_z\left(q C - K_{\mathrm{disp}}\partial_z C\right)\) for \(\mathrm{NO_3^-}\)-N and DOC-C, verifying \(M^{n+1} - M^n - (F_{\mathrm{top}} - F_{\mathrm{bot}})\Delta t = 0\).

Freundlich equilibrium-sorption index-1 descriptor DAE (EquilibriumSorptionFunctor, Level 2)

relic.scientific.pedosphere.transport.equilibrium_sorption.EquilibriumSorptionFunctor (Level 2, PhysicalFieldFunctor) formulates nonlinear Freundlich equilibrium sorption \(S = K_f C^n\) (\(n \in [0.3, 1.0]\)) with first-order dissolved-phase degradation rate \(\lambda \ge 0\) (Jury and Horton, 2004; Mayes et al., 2012; Hairer and Wanner, 1996) as a semi-explicit index-1 descriptor DAE \(E\dot{\mathbf{x}} = \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x})\), \(\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{0}\) on \(\mathbf{x} = (y, C, S)^{\mathsf{T}}\) with \(E = \operatorname{diag}(1, 0, 0)\):

\[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = -\lambda\,\theta\,C, \qquad g_1(y, C, S) = \theta C + \rho_b S - y = 0, \qquad g_2(C, S) = S - K_f C^n = 0. \]

Because \(\partial_C(\theta C + \rho_b K_f C^n - y) = \theta + \rho_b K_f n C^{n-1} > 0\) for \(\theta > 0\) and \(C > 0\), the algebraic Jacobian is strictly positive (differentiation index 1). At every step (including post-checkpoint restart validation of the stored \((y, C, S)\) triple), implicit backward-Euler elimination solves the strictly monotone scalar equation

\[ F(C') = \theta(1 + \lambda\,\Delta t)C' + \rho_b K_f (C')^n - y = 0, \qquad C' \in \left[0,\; \frac{y}{\theta}\right], \]

via relic.computation.solvers.nonlinear.BracketedBisectionSolver, updates differential total mass \(y' = y - \lambda\,\theta\,C'\Delta t\) via UpdateItem(ACCUMULATE, per_timestep=True), and replaces algebraic states \(C'\) and \(S' = K_f (C')^n\) (REPLACE), reporting the post-step manifold residual \(\lvert \theta C' + \rho_b S' - y' \rvert\).

1D ALE moving-domain diffusion and exact GCL (MovingDomainDiffusionFunctor, Level 3)

relic.scientific.pedosphere.transport.moving_domain_diffusion.MovingDomainDiffusionFunctor (Level 3, TransportMechanismFunctor) solves Fickian solute diffusion on a uniformly stretching or compressing 1D column \(x(\xi, t) = \xi L(t)\), \(\xi \in [0, 1]\), driven by lower-boundary velocity \(w_b\) [m s\(^{-1}\)] (Thomas and Lombard, 1979; Donea et al., 2004). With \(N\) uniform cells of thickness \(V_i(t) = \Delta x(t) = L(t)/N\) and face velocities \(w_k = (k/N)w_b\) (\(k = 0, \dots, N\)), the discrete Geometric Conservation Law (GCL) holds identically:

\[ V_i(t + \Delta t) - V_i(t) = \Delta t\,(w_{i+1} - w_i) = \frac{w_b\,\Delta t}{N}, \qquad L(t + \Delta t) = L(t) + w_b\,\Delta t. \]

Subject to both diffusive Von Neumann and mesh-Courant (\(\lvert w_b \rvert \Delta t / \Delta x \le \mathrm{CFL}_{\mathrm{mesh,max}}\)) bounds, cell solute mass \(m_i = V_i c_i\) advances by zero-flux interior diffusion plus upwind relative swept-face fluxes \(s_k = c_{\mathrm{face},k} w_k\) (entraining exterior concentration \(c_b\) when \(w_b > 0\) and exporting bottom-cell \(c_{N-1}\) when \(w_b < 0\)):

\[ m_i(t + \Delta t) = m_i(t) + \Delta t\left(r_{\mathrm{diff},i}\,\Delta x(t) + s_{i+1} - s_i\right), \qquad c_i(t + \Delta t) = \frac{m_i(t + \Delta t)}{V_i(t + \Delta t)}. \]

On the time-dependent Hodge metric \(\star(t) = \operatorname{diag}(L(t)/N)\) with quadratic storage \(H = \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{c}^{\mathsf{T}}\star(t)\mathbf{c}\) and \(\dot{\star} = \operatorname{diag}(w_b / N)\), the moving-geometry power term \(-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{c}^{\mathsf{T}}\dot{\star}\mathbf{c}\) is emitted explicitly in diagnostics.moving_domain.geometry_power alongside gcl_residual and mass_balance_residual.

Mobile-immobile exact exponential memory exchange (TwoRegionMassTransferFunctor, Level 3)

relic.scientific.pedosphere.transport.two_region_mass_transfer.TwoRegionMassTransferFunctor (Level 3, TransportMechanismFunctor) implements first-order mass transfer of rate \(\alpha > 0\) [s\(^{-1}\)] between mobile (\(\theta_m, c_m\)) and stagnant immobile (\(\theta_{\mathrm{im}}, c_{\mathrm{im}}\)) pore-water regions (van Genuchten and Wierenga, 1976; Haggerty and Gorelick, 1995). On the \(\theta\)-weighted storage state \(\mathbf{x} = (\theta_m c_m, \theta_{\mathrm{im}} c_{\mathrm{im}})^{\mathsf{T}}\) with quadratic free-energy proxy \(H(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{2}(\theta_m c_m^2 + \theta_{\mathrm{im}} c_{\mathrm{im}}^2)\) and conjugate effort \(\mathbf{e} = \frac{\partial H}{\partial \mathbf{x}} = (c_m, c_{\mathrm{im}})^{\mathsf{T}}\), the dynamics form a purely dissipative system (\(J_h = 0\)):

\[\begin{split} \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{x}}{\mathrm{d}t} = -R_h\mathbf{e}, \qquad R_h = \alpha \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \succeq 0, \qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}t} = -\alpha(c_m - c_{\mathrm{im}})^2 \le 0. \end{split}\]

Eliminating \(c_{\mathrm{im}}\) yields the passive exponential Volterra memory kernel \(K(t) = \alpha\omega\exp(-\omega t)\) with \(\omega = \alpha / \theta_{\mathrm{im}}\). Over each step \(\Delta t\), TwoRegionMassTransferFunctor advances the linear \(2 \times 2\) exchange analytically via its exact matrix exponential \(c_m(t+\Delta t) - c_{\mathrm{im}}(t+\Delta t) = (c_m(t) - c_{\mathrm{im}}(t))\exp(-\kappa \Delta t)\) with \(\kappa = \alpha(\theta_m^{-1} + \theta_{\mathrm{im}}^{-1})\), conserving total pore solute \(\theta_m \Delta c_m + \theta_{\mathrm{im}}\Delta c_{\mathrm{im}} = 0\) to machine precision and declaring relic.core.functor.SubFlowAccuracy.EXACT on its state update.
